items.text: Cyber is going to be one of the most profound aspects of AI. We now have a tireless workforce that can hunt down, discover, patch, or attack any system and software ever created. items.title: How a Frontier Team Can Help Your Company Keep Up With AI
items.text: You need a frontier team. Here's why. Every single person in your company is caught in this dilemma. Do I get my work done or do I stay up to date with AI and figure out what all these new tools and workflows mean for what work I should do? That's just crazy. It's so hard to figure out. Every single company is struggling with this right now. Because, I mean, on the one hand, you could ignore the frontier and that'll probably work for a little while until you get disrupted by some agent native version of your product that you didn't see coming. Or you can keep up with the frontier and just chase shiny objects and never build anything that lasts. The reason why you need a frontier team is it separates things out. items.text: If you wanted to know all the jobs that AI will produce, look no further than cybersecurity. This is going to become one of the biggest investment areas for enterprises going forward. And even as the work becomes more agentic and autonomous you will need more talent to point the agents at the most critical work, review findings, patch systems, respond to incidents, and more. Lots of opportunity right now for the systems that protect data and enterprises, as well as the professionals that are deploying them and protecting organizations. It’s going to only get more wild out there.

items.title: I'm still grokking this
items.text: I'm still grokking this...but it does feel like it just as fun to make stuff with AI as it is to "use" it. My son watched Star Wars (EP IV) for ~3 hours...but then spent ~20 hours making games about what he had seen. But weirdly, he only played the games a little bit...he was more interested in just building the game. As a programmer, I understand parts of this intuitively...the very act of programming is fun (most of the time). And I have always felt bad for people who couldn't experience that joy... But maybe everyone will now get to experience that?
